sys_script.description: Issues the claim number from the sys_number counter on insert, for every submission path. Replaces the unreachable global getNextObjNumberPadded dictionary default. Never overwrites a number that was supplied deliberately.
sys_script.name: ClaimEase - Assign Claim Number

sys_script.description: Applies the rolling-window duplicate rule to small claims entering submitted, after taking a per-employee database-enforced mutex so two simultaneous qualifying submissions cannot both pass. On a hit the claim is recorded as a duplicate and no approval process is started.
sys_script.name: ClaimEase - Duplicate Guard

sys_script.description: Forces submitted_by to the authenticated user on insert, sets submitted_on the first time the claim is submitted, refreshes last_status_update when approval_status changes, populates manager from the employee record with a fallback to the exception queue, and captures the manager and finance decision stamps.
sys_script.name: ClaimEase - Lifecycle Stamps

sys_script.description: Converts the claim amount into the configured base currency and stores it in amount_usd, the only field used for threshold and duplicate evaluation. Aborts the save when conversion is impossible.
sys_script.name: ClaimEase - Normalise Amount

sys_script.description: Rejects unauthorised changes to manager_approval and finance_approval, freezes amount, amount_usd and requested_for once the claim has left draft (admins excepted), and rejects invalid approval transitions.
sys_script.name: ClaimEase - Protect Approval Fields

sys_script.description: Releases the per-employee submission mutex acquired by the Duplicate Guard, once the claim row has committed and is visible to other transactions. No-op when no lock is held.
sys_script.name: ClaimEase - Release Submission Lock
sys_script.script: /** * ClaimEase - Release Submission Lock (after insert/update, order 1000) * * PURPOSE * Releases the per-employee submission mutex that the "Duplicate Guard" * before-rule acquired. * * The release MUST happen here rather than at the end of the duplicate guard. * The guard runs before the claim row is written, so releasing there would let * a second transaction acquire the lock and run its duplicate query before the * first claim became visible — re-opening exactly the race the lock exists to * close. By the time an after-rule runs, the claim is committed and visible, * so it is safe to let the next submission through. * * Runs at order 1000 so it is the last thing to happen on the save. * * SAFETY * - The lock is keyed by employee and owned by this claim's sys_id, so this * rule can only ever release a lock that this claim took. * - It is a harmless no-op when no lock is held (the common case: large * claims, draft saves, approval updates). * - If a transaction aborts between the guard and this rule, the lock's * `expires_on` lets the next acquirer reclaim it, so no employee can be * blocked indefinitely. */ ;(function executeRule() { var duplicateCheck = new ClaimEaseDuplicateCheck() duplicateCheck.releaseSubmissionLock(current.getValue('requested_for'), current.getUniqueValue()) })()

sys_script.description: Sets flow_started true on a submitted, non-duplicate claim, in the same transaction as the save. This is the flag the Flow Designer approval flow triggers on, for both record creation and the draft-to-submitted update. A no-op when the claim is not submitted, is already started, or was blocked as a duplicate.
sys_script.name: ClaimEase - Start Approval Process

sys_script.description: Runs ClaimEaseValidator for every interface, adds friendly error messages and aborts the save when the claim is invalid. The receipt requirement is enforced on the transition into submitted, not on insert.
sys_script.name: ClaimEase - Validate Claim
